response.sql: WITH groups AS (SELECT ID, COUNT(*) AS cnt, CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Examination) AS frac FROM Examination GROUP BY ID), avg_frac AS (SELECT AVG(frac) AS avg_frac FROM groups) SELECT g.ID, g.cnt AS num_examinations, g.frac AS fraction, g.frac - a.avg_frac AS excess FROM groups g CROSS JOIN avg_frac a WHERE g.frac > a.avg_frac ORDER BY excess DESC LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: Examination rows with a NULL ID form a single group, which GROUP BY ID produces automatically; the fraction denominator is the total row count of Examination, including NULL-ID rows.
The average fraction is the unweighted mean of the per-group fractions (each group counts once), not a mean weighted by examination count.
Fractions and excesses are unrounded REAL values, as the request specifies.
Groups with equal excess have no specified order, so their order in the top 10 is arbitrary.
